guideTitle: The Best Portable Monitors Under $200 for Work and Travel
metaDescription: Under $200, portable monitors trade size, sharpness and refresh rate. We compared eight 15.6- to 18.5-inch models on resolution, refresh, inputs, weight and stand.
introParagraphs: A portable monitor adds a second screen to a laptop anywhere. Under $200, the trade-offs are size (15.6 to 18.5 inches), sharpness (1080p or 2.5K), refresh rate (60 to 144Hz) and how it stands, from folding covers to kickstands and VESA mounts.

Check connections first. A single USB-C cable can carry video and power only if your laptop's USB-C port supports video output; otherwise you'll use HDMI plus a USB power cable. Mini-HDMI needs a specific cable.
Every monitor here was under $200 at the time of writing, most under $125. Our comparison is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing.

kyy-156-under200.summary: A 15.6-inch 1080p IPS monitor with two USB-C and mini-HDMI inputs and a cover stand, 1.7 lb.
kyy-156-under200.description:
The KYY is a sensible everyday portable monitor: a 15.6-inch 1080p IPS panel, two USB-C ports and a mini-HDMI input, a cover that doubles as a stand at two fixed angles, and a 1.7 lb weight.

It was one of the lower-priced monitors here at the time of writing. The cover stand offers only two angles, and mini-HDMI needs a specific cable.
kyy-156-under200.bestFor: A laptop second screen for travel and everyday work.
kyy-156-under200.skipIf: You want a sharper screen; the ARZOPA 16-inch 2.5K has 2560 x 1600.

mnn-156-under200.summary: A 15.6-inch 1080p 60Hz monitor with dual USB-C, HDMI and an HDR mode, the cheapest here.
mnn-156-under200.description:
The MNN is the least expensive monitor here, about $50 at the time of writing: a 15.6-inch 1080p 60Hz panel with dual USB-C, HDMI, several display modes and an HDR mode.

An HDR mode on a budget panel is unlikely to match true HDR displays, and brightness isn't stated.
mnn-156-under200.bestFor: A basic second screen for as little as possible.
mnn-156-under200.skipIf: You want better color; the EVICIV lists 125% sRGB.

eviciv-185-under200.summary: An 18.5-inch 120Hz monitor with 125% sRGB, FreeSync, full-size HDMI and VESA.
eviciv-185-under200.description:
The EVICIV offers the largest screen here, 18.5 inches, at 120Hz with FreeSync and a listed 125% sRGB color range, plus full-size HDMI, dual USB-C, a 75mm VESA mount and a 360-degree bracket.

Its size makes it less portable, closer to a compact desk monitor you can move.
eviciv-185-under200.bestFor: A movable second screen on a desk, or light gaming.
eviciv-185-under200.skipIf: You travel often; a 15.6-inch model is lighter.

arzopa-16-under200.summary: A 16-inch 2560 x 1600 IPS monitor, 350 nits, 123% sRGB, 1.46 lb.
arzopa-16-under200.description:
The ARZOPA 16-inch 2.5K is the sharpest option here with a clear resolution: 2560 x 1600 on a 16-inch 16:10 panel, rated at 350 nits and 123% sRGB, weighing 1.46 lb, with USB-C and HDMI.

Its refresh rate isn't stated in the summary, so assume 60Hz unless the listing says otherwise.
arzopa-16-under200.skipIf: You want high refresh; the cocopar 2.5K adds 144Hz.

innoview-16-under200.summary: A 16-inch 120Hz monitor listed at 2160 x 1600, 100% sRGB; power adapter not included.
innoview-16-under200.description:
The InnoView pairs a 16-inch panel with 120Hz and 100% sRGB, at a lower price than the other 2.5K monitors at the time of writing, with dual USB-C and HDMI and a lightweight stand.

The listing gives 2160 x 1600, an unusual figure that may be a typo for 2560 x 1600; confirm before buying. A power adapter isn't included, which you may need for HDMI use.
innoview-16-under200.skipIf: You need a clearly stated resolution; the ARZOPA 2.5K lists 2560 x 1600.

cocopar-156-under200.summary: A 15.6-inch 1080p 60Hz monitor with full-size HDMI, dual USB-C and VESA holes.
cocopar-156-under200.description:
The cocopar 15.6-inch is a straightforward 1080p 60Hz monitor with an 85% sRGB listing, full-size HDMI, dual USB-C and VESA mounting holes, useful for fixing it to an arm.

It cost about as much as the higher-spec InnoView at the time of writing, so its VESA mount and brand feedback are the reasons to choose it.
cocopar-156-under200.bestFor: Mounting a portable monitor on an arm.
cocopar-156-under200.skipIf: You want more for the money; the InnoView adds 120Hz.

arzopa-161-144-under200.summary: A 16.1-inch 1080p 144Hz monitor with 106% sRGB and a built-in kickstand.
arzopa-161-144-under200.description:
The ARZOPA 16.1-inch runs at 144Hz, the highest refresh among the 1080p monitors here, with 106% sRGB listed, two USB-C and mini-HDMI inputs and a built-in kickstand, under $100 at the time of writing.

The listing doesn't mention adaptive sync, which helps smooth games with varying frame rates.
arzopa-161-144-under200.bestFor: Console or laptop gaming on the go.
arzopa-161-144-under200.skipIf: You want FreeSync; the EVICIV lists it.

cocopar-16-under200.summary: A 16-inch 2.5K monitor with 144Hz over USB-C, 120Hz over HDMI, 110% sRGB and a metal chassis.
cocopar-16-under200.description:
The cocopar 16-inch 2.5K combines sharpness and speed: a 2.5K panel at 144Hz over USB-C or 120Hz over HDMI, 110% sRGB, a metal chassis, full-size HDMI, dual USB-C and VESA holes.

It was the most expensive monitor here at the time of writing, close to the $200 ceiling.
cocopar-16-under200.bestFor: Sharp text and smooth motion in one monitor.
cocopar-16-under200.skipIf: Budget matters; the ARZOPA 144Hz costs much less at 1080p.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Single-cable use needs video output (DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt).
2.5K (ARZOPA 16, cocopar 16) is sharper for text than 1080p.
60Hz suits office work; 120–144Hz suits gaming and smooth scrolling.
18.5 inches is less portable; VESA holes allow arm mounting.

faq.q: Can one USB-C cable run it?
faq.a: Yes, if your laptop's USB-C port supports video output and enough power.
2.5K is noticeably sharper for text on a 16-inch screen; 1080p costs less.
For gaming or smooth motion; office work is fine at 60Hz.

faq.q: Can I mount it on an arm?
faq.a: The models with VESA holes, such as the cocopar and EVICIV, can be mounted.

faq.q: Will it work with a phone or console?
faq.a: Many support USB-C or HDMI sources; check the listing for your device.

bottomLine: For most laptop users, the KYY 15.6-inch is an inexpensive everyday second screen, and the ARZOPA 16-inch 2.5K is worth a little more for sharper text.
For gaming, the ARZOPA 144Hz is the value pick and the cocopar 16-inch 2.5K 144Hz the high-end option. The EVICIV suits a movable desk screen.
